title: Is AI interpretability close to a breakthrough? A new essay has researchers divided
key_facts: Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the interpretability lab Goodfire, published an essay titled "Neural Networks Are Already Clean".
He argues that the inner workings of large AI models are much easier to understand than assumed and rejects the superposition explanation he helped shape.
He reinterprets the famous cat-and-car neuron in InceptionV1 as a V-shape detector, not a mix of unrelated concepts.
For Qwen3-32B he gives preliminary numbers: about 90 percent of neuron poles have one main job, about 7 percent have two related ones, 2 to 4 percent are unexplained.
Goodfire says it sees similar results in models with up to trillions of parameters; AI agents analysing neurons in bulk did most of the work.
Roon, an OpenAI employee who posts under that pseudonym on X, called it a possible major moment in scientific history but said others still need to confirm the results.
Neel Nanda, who leads the interpretability team at Google DeepMind, says the work is interesting but does not really change the big picture and that neuron-based analysis will miss a lot.
The technical companion paper has not been released yet and Goodfire has a stake in the thesis.
